what: First-time visitors only. On the white curtain covering the hero, a character sequence (single-row sprite, 15 frames by default) flips between two frames (4 and 5) with no in-between values every .48s and stays for 3s, then the curtain background and greeting text lift away over .9s cubic-bezier(.25,1,.5,1) and fx:open fires. Wheel and touch scroll are blocked until it lifts. The sequence stays in place after the curtain lifts (character sitting on a river) and keeps swaying, and fx:sprite plays other sequences once, like climbing on or diving in. If already seen this session, fx:open fires right away with no curtain

options.frames: Sprite frame count, default 15 — strip width grows to frames × window width
options.seq: Cell numbers to repeat above and behind the curtain (space-separated), default ”4 5” — original moritoLoop (.96s steps(1) two cells)
options.hold · fade: Duration the curtain stays and duration it lifts (seconds), default 3 · .9 — shorten for screens opened often, like apps
options.key: sessionStorage name that records what was already seen, default fx-sprite-curtain-opening
options.lock: If off, scrolling is not blocked while the overlay is shown
options.--fx-veil · --fx-ease · --fx-pad: Curtain color (default --kf-surface) · reveal curve · offset below the continuous image (default 26svh) (via style)
options.[data-fx-part=window] > [data-fx-part=st: A one-cell window (width and height given by the user) and a horizontal strip inside it (one svg or img, cells side by side from the left)
options.[data-fx-part=greet]: Greeting text that lifts with the curtain (optional)
options.fx:sprite: on el, CustomEvent('fx:sprite', { detail: { seq: '0 1 2 3 4', beat: .21, then: 'idle' | 'hold' } }) — after running the sequence once, it returns to looping (idle) or stops at the last cell (hold)

use: Your short greeting here
note: The original chains frame advance with CSS steps(1) keyframes (percent frame positions) and the curtain lifting with the transitionend of a background-color transition. The part generalizes frame advance into an interval timer and the end of the lift into a hold+fade timer. For sequences with uneven frame dwell (original moritoFirst 4.2s · moritoLast 3.6s), keeping them as site-side keyframes gives the same numbers.

from.where: index.html .p-top-fv__chara (white veil) + .p-top-fv__sprite (mascot, 15 cells) — original .p-top-fv__chara background-color .9s cubic-bezier(.25,1,.5,1) 3s · ::before greeting text with the same values · chara-img 79.3×29.3rem window with a 1190rem strip, moritoLoop .96s steps(1) infinite (cells 4·5), html.change on transitionend and Swiper autoplay 1.5s later, skipped via sessionStorage animationPlayed, wheel·touchmove preventDefault while the veil is up
